mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, والذاريات فَالْحَامِلَات فالجاريان فَالْمُقَسِّمَات: all of these are adjectives standing in place of a described thing sworn by, on the assumption of the oath being by its Creator and Mover, who is Allah, there is no god but He. Its implied form is "By the Lord of the winds that scatter, then the clouds that carry a load, then the ships that run, then the angels that apportion" (ورب الرياح الذاريات فالسحاب الحاملات وقرا فالسفن الجاريات فالملائكة المقسمات). And the answer [to the oath] is إنما توعدون لصادق. [Translator's note: «فالجاريان» is as printed in the edition; the Quranic word is فالجاريات.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying يسرا: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "an easy running" (جريا يسرا).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying يَوْم هم على النَّار يفتنون: يوم is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because its annexation is not genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), since it is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin). Its position is accusative in the sense of "the recompense is on the day they are tried over the Fire" (الجزاء يوم هم على النار يفتنون). It is also said that its position is nominative as a badal (substitute) of يوم الدين. It is also said that it is accusative and not indeclinable, and its accusative is by an implied [word], its implied form being "the recompense is on the day they..." (الجزاء يوم هم).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying كَانُوا قَلِيلا من اللَّيْل مَا يهجعون: the noun of كان is the latent pronoun in it, which is the wāw; يهجعون is the khabar (predicate) of كان; and قليلا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverb, its implied form being "they used to sleep a little time" (كانوا وقتا قليلا يهجعون) or "they used to sleep a little sleep" (هجوعا قليلا يهجعون); and ما is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.
If you wish, you may make ما together with the verb a maṣdar in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in كان, with قليلا as the khabar of كان; its implied form is "their sleeping at night was little" (كان هجوعهم من الليل قليلا). If you wish, you may make the maṣdar nominative by قليل [as its agent] and put قليلا in the accusative as the khabar of كان.
It is not permissible to make قليلا accusative by يهجعون unless ما is redundant, because if you made it accusative by يهجعون while ما with the verb is a maṣdar, you would have put the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative.
It is also possible that قليلا is the khabar of كان, its noun being in it, and ما negating; this is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and pausing on قليلا is then good; it is the view of Yaʿqūb and others. One does not pause on قليل on the earlier views.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {إِنَّه لحق مثل مَا أَنكُمْ تنطقون}: whoever reads مثلَ in the accusative made it indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its annexation to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin), namely أنكم, with ما redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. It is also said that it is indeclinable on the fatḥa because مثل and ما are one noun; when the two were made one thing, مثل was made indeclinable on the fatḥa; this is the view of al-Māzinī. It is also said that مثلا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of an indefinite, namely لحق; this is the view of al-Jarmī. It is also said that it is a ḥāl of the nominative latent pronoun in His saying لحق, with ما redundant and مثل annexed to أنكم; it did not take full declension because of its annexation to something not fully declinable, and it is a non-genuine annexation. Some of the Kufans said مثل is accusative by the omission of the كاف, its implied form being "it is truly real, like what you speak" (إنه لحق كمثل ما أنكم تنطقون), with ما redundant, its implied form being "like your speaking" (كمثل نطقكم); and that is not permissible according to the Basrans. Abū Muḥammad [i.e. Makkī] said: whoever reads the accusative, it is possible that it is by way of emphasis, in the sense "it is truly real, as real as your speaking" (إنه لحق حقا مثل نطقكم).
As for whoever reads مثلُ in the nominative, he made it an adjective of حق, because it is indefinite, since its annexation is not genuine, because the respects in which likeness occurs between two things that resemble each other are many; therefore it did not become definite by its annexation to أنكم. Since it did not become definite, it was good to describe حق with it, just as you say مررت برجل مثلك ("I passed by a man like you"). On these views أنكم is in the position of the genitive by مثل, and it together with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is "it is truly real, like your speaking" (إنه لحق مثل نطقكم).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying قَالُوا سَلاما: سلام is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or because the saying falls upon it [as its object].
His saying قَالَ سَلام: a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "he said: peace be upon you" (قال سلام عليكم). It is also said that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "my affair is peace" (أمري سلام). Whoever reads سِلْم takes it on the assumption "we are peace(ful)" (نحن سلم); it is also said that it means سلام, just as one says حِلّ and حلال with the same meaning.
His saying وَقَالَت عَجُوز عقيم: عجوز is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "I am an old woman" (أنا عجوز).

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying وَقوم نوح: whoever reads قوم in the genitive conjoins it to His saying وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا; it is also said that it is conjoined to وفي موسى; and it is also said: to وفي الأرض. Whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to the هاء and the ميم in His saying فأخذتهم; it is also said that its implied form is "and We destroyed the people of Noah" (وأهلكنا قوم نوح); it is also said: in the sense of "and remember the people of Noah" (واذكر قوم نوح); it is also said that it is conjoined to فأخذناه; and it is also said: to فنبذناهم.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying كَذَلِك مَا أَتَى: the كاف is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is thus" (الأمر كذلك). It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying المتين: a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of إنّ. It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of الرزاق, or of ذو القوة, or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a naʿt of the noun of إنّ according to its position. Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt of القوة, and it is masculine because [القوة] is not a real feminine.
